summary: Backend-only retest of the intelligent VIN→vehicle_id picker fix (rapidapi_client.vin_mega_decode now unwraps payload['data']). 5/5 pytest cases passed: (1) vin_mega_decode(VR7EF9HNAKJ575626) returns dict with sra_commercial='1.6 HDI 75 (MF9HW, GJ9HWC, GF9HWC, GN9HWC)'; (2) pick_best_vehicle_id over real TecDoc list for model_id=39023 with that sra returns 133257; (3) sanity unit test confirming BlueHDi→HDi token normalisation picks the 75 hp variant over 100 hp; (4) GET /api/oem-stock-search with VIN+model_id=39023+q='filtre à huile' returns 200 after wiping tecdoc_vehicle_cache; (5) backend log contains 'VIN VR7EF9HNAKJ575626: matched vehicle_id=133257 via sra=...' as expected.

minor.issue: When the picker fails to match, code silently falls back to vehicles[0].get('vehicleId') with only an info log. Consider returning the fallback flag (e.g. 'matched_by_vin': false) in the response so the frontend can warn the user.

Function returns the inner 'data' dict when present, but if a future RapidAPI response wraps data differently (e.g. data.vehicle.sra_commercial) the unwrap is one level only. Worth adding a debug log of payload top-level keys when sra_commercial is missing, to aid future debugging.

Scoring only accepts the strongest match (every sra token present). If sra contains an extra token absent from all typeEngineName variants (e.g. region marker), no vehicle is ever picked. A partial-best fallback (≥ N-1 tokens) would be more forgiving.
Cache key includes vin, model_id, lang_id but no TTL/expiry. If TecDoc updates variants, stale cache rows can return obsolete vehicle_ids forever. Add a 7-day TTL index or invalidation strategy.

action_items: OPTIONAL — Expose 'matched_by_vin' / 'vehicle_id_source' in /api/oem-stock-search response so the UI can show whether the engine variant was chosen via VIN or fell back to the first one.
OPTIONAL — Add TTL on tecdoc_vehicle_cache so stale entries expire.
OPTIONAL — Add a debug log of payload keys in vin_mega_decode when 'sra_commercial' is absent.
critical_code_review_comments: Fix is correct and minimal: payload.get('data') unwrap in vin_mega_decode is the right surgical change.
_engine_tokens does only one normalisation (Blue/e prefix strip). Robust enough for the current VW/PSA test cases but won't catch e.g. 'CDTi' (Opel) ↔ 'Common Rail Diesel'. Keep an eye on it.
server.py is now 1564 lines — past the 700-line guideline. Strong candidate for splitting into auth/catalog/orders/admin/oem routers when feasible.
pick_best_vehicle_id returns None on no full match — caller correctly handles fallback to vehicles[0]; behaviour matches review_request expectation.

Cache write happens AFTER successful resolution only — good; failed matches won't poison the cache. But note resolved vehicle_id is cached regardless of whether it came from VIN match or fallback; consider keying with 'source' for clarity.
test_credentials: Admin: admin@bennouri.com / Admin@123. New test users created on-the-fly with TEST_vin_* prefix.
seed_data_creation: Each run registers 1 fresh user TEST_vin_<uuid>@example.com (used only for JWT). One row may be inserted into tecdoc_vehicle_cache for {vin:VR7EF9HNAKJ575626, model_id:39023, lang_id:6}.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The VIN→vehicle_id fix is verified end-to-end against the real RapidAPI vin-decoder-mega + auto-parts-catalog (TecDoc) endpoints. To re-verify on a cold cache, delete the cached row first: db.tecdoc_vehicle_cache.delete_many({'vin':'VR7EF9HNAKJ575626'}). Backend log line 'VIN <vin>: matched vehicle_id=<id> via sra=<sra>' is the canonical signal that the intelligent picker fired. The same test file also asserts the fallback (cache wipe → fresh resolution).
rca of the issue: Original bug: rapidapi_client.vin_mega_decode returned the outer envelope dict (e.g. {'data': {...}, 'status': 'ok'}), so .get('sra_commercial') was always None and the picker received an empty string → it returned None → server fell back to vehicles[0] (wrong variant). Fix in vin_mega_decode (lines 128-132): after parsing JSON, if payload['data'] is a dict, return that inner dict; else return payload as-is. Verified: live RapidAPI call now yields sra_commercial='1.6 HDI 75 (MF9HW, GJ9HWC, GF9HWC, GN9HWC)' and the picker selects vehicleId=133257 against TecDoc model 39023 — matching the user-reported expected value. The supervisor log confirms: 'VIN VR7EF9HNAKJ575626: matched vehicle_id=133257 via sra=...'.
